text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Secret deal lifts Alberta MDs' cap: Klein government quietly offered to inject up to C$50 million into fees 9 days before vote.
- Liberals may duck selection process: PM will hand-pick some candidates.
- Israeli pullout plan rejected: Small-scale retreat riles Palestinians.
- Albanian leader announces unity accord: Political foes says agreement is good but doubts whether it will be respected.
- Reconciliation eludes two solitudes: One year after Quebec Premier Lucien Bouchard reached out to the province's anglophones, four major problems remain.
- U.S. economy still on a roll: Fed boss may be tempted to raise rates to ensure inflationary pressures are kept in check.
- No long lineup to buy Eaton's: U.S. chains not eager to acquire ailing company.
- Fletcher's new challenge: Observers ponder how TimberWest cash to be used.
- The Street's divided on energy plays.
- Wall Street's steamroller heads up Bay Street.
- Eaton's suppliers push for fast restructuring.
- Corel fights time and a jittery market.
